title: Investments, Topic 1: formulas and calculations
focus: Formula recall first, then calculation drills. Open the formula sheet only after you try.
sheet:
Formulas

  • HPR = (ending - starting + dividends) / starting
  • Annualised = (1 + HPR)^(12 / months held) - 1
  • Arithmetic average = sum of returns / n
  • Geometric average = [(1+r1)(1+r2)...(1+rn)]^(1/n) - 1 (always at most the arithmetic)
  • Dollar-weighted return = IRR of the investor's cash flows
  • z = (x - mean) / standard deviation. About 68% lies within one standard deviation of the mean.

Memory hooks

  • HPR: gain over cost. The bottom is always what you paid.
  • Annualising exponent = how many of these periods fit in a year (12 divided by months).
  • Geometric: multiply (1 + r), take the nth root, subtract 1.
  • z-score: distance from the mean, counted in standard deviations.

qs.q: Which formula gives the holding period return (HPR)?
o: (ending price - starting price + dividends) / starting price
(ending price - starting price - dividends) / starting price
qs.exp: HPR = gain over cost = (ending - starting + dividends) / starting. Divide by what you paid, and add dividends to the gain.

qs.q: Which formula annualises a holding period return?
qs.exp: Annualised = (1 + HPR)^(12 / months held) - 1. The exponent asks: how many of these periods fit in a year? A 3-month return repeats 4 times, so the exponent is 12/3 = 4.

qs.q: Which formula gives the geometric average return over n years?
qs.exp: Geometric: multiply the growth factors (1 + r), take the nth root (power 1/n), then subtract 1 to get back to a return.

qs.q: Which formula gives the z-score of a value x?
qs.exp: z = (x - mean) / standard deviation. It tells you how many standard deviations x is from the mean. About 68% of outcomes lie within one standard deviation either side of the mean.

qs.q: The dollar-weighted return is:
o: The IRR of the investor's cash flows
The geometric average of yearly returns
The HPR divided by the number of years
qs.exp: Dollar-weighted return = the IRR of the investor's own cash flows, so it depends on when money goes in and out.

qs.q: Returns vary from year to year. How do the geometric and arithmetic averages compare?
o: Geometric is lower than or equal to arithmetic
qs.exp: Geometric is less than or equal to arithmetic. They are equal only if every return is the same. Losses shrink the base later gains compound on.

qs.q: You buy a stock at $25.00, receive a $0.50 dividend and sell at $26.75. What is the holding period return (%)? Give 2 decimal places.
qs.hint: Step 1: gain = ending - starting + dividends. Step 2: divide by starting price.

qs.q: You buy a stock at $8.40, receive a $0.20 dividend and sell at $7.56. What is the holding period return (%)? Give 2 decimal places. Use a minus sign for a loss.
qs.exp: HPR = (7.56 - 8.40 + 0.20) / 8.40 = -0.64 / 8.40 = -7.62%. The price fell 0.84 and the dividend gives back 0.20.

qs.q: A 3-month holding period return is 2%. What is the annualised return (%)? Give 2 decimal places.
qs.exp: Exponent = 12 / 3 = 4. Annualised = 1.02^4 - 1 = 1.0824 - 1 = 8.24%. Note this is more than 2% x 4 = 8% because of compounding.

qs.q: An 8-month holding period return is 12%. What is the annualised return (%)? Give 2 decimal places.
A 24-month holding period return is 6%. What is the annualised return (%)? Give 2 decimal places.
qs.exp: Exponent = 12 / 24 = 0.5. Annualised = 1.06^0.5 - 1 = 1.0296 - 1 = 2.96%. Longer than a year means the exponent is below 1.

qs.q: You buy a stock at $40.00, receive a $1.00 dividend and sell it at $42.50 after 6 months. What is the annualised return (%)? Give 2 decimal places.
A fund returned +12%, -6%, +9% and +3% in four years. What is the arithmetic average return (%)? Give 2 decimal places.
The same fund returned +12%, -6%, +9% and +3%. What is the geometric average return (%)? Give 2 decimal places.
An investment returns +50% in year 1 and -50% in year 2. What is the geometric average return per year (%)? Give 2 decimal places. Use a minus sign for a loss.
qs.exp: Geometric = (1.50 x 0.50)^(1/2) - 1 = 0.75^0.5 - 1 = 0.8660 - 1 = -13.40%. The arithmetic average is 0%, which hides the fact that $100 ends at $75.

qs.q: An investor puts in $1,000 now, receives $100 at the end of year 1 and $1,100 at the end of year 2 (final sale). What is the dollar-weighted return, the IRR (%)? Give 2 decimal places.
qs.exp: Try 10%: 100 / 1.10 + 1,100 / 1.10^2 = 90.91 + 909.09 = 1,000. So the IRR is 10.00%. IRR is the rate that makes the present value of inflows equal the amount invested.

qs.q: Returns are normal with mean 9% and standard deviation 5%. What is the z-score for a return of -1%? Give 2 decimal places.
Returns are normal with mean 6% and standard deviation 10%. Using the 68% rule, what is the upper end (%) of the range that contains about 68% of outcomes?
qs.exp: 68% lies within one standard deviation of the mean: 6 +/- 10 gives -4% to 16%. The upper end is 16%.

qs.q: Returns are normal with mean 6% and standard deviation 10%. Using the 68% rule, what is the probability (%) of a return above 16%? Round to a whole number.
qs.exp: 16% is one standard deviation above the mean. 68% is inside, so 32% is outside, and half of that, 16%, is in the upper tail.

qs.q: A company's CEO resigns suddenly and its share price falls while the market is flat. What type of risk is this?
o: Interest rate risk for all stocks
qs.exp: It affects one company, so it is unsystematic and can be reduced by diversification. A market-wide rate rise is systematic.

title: Commercial Banking, Topic 2: loan formulas and calculations
focus: Formula recall first, then fixed instalment and fixed principal drills. Open the formula sheet only after you try.
sheet:
Steps for every loan question

  1. r = annual rate / 12, n = years x 12.
  2. Decide: equal instalments or fixed principal?
  3. Then use the right formula.

Fixed instalment (equal payments)

  • A = P x r / [1 - (1 + r)^-n]
  • Total interest = A x n - P (subtract P)

Fixed principal

  • R = P / n
  • Instalment in a month = R + balance before that payment x r
  • First = R + P x r. Last = R + R x r.
  • Total interest = r x R x n(n+1)/2, or (first interest + last interest) / 2 x n

Memory hooks

  • Two steps always come first: r and n in months.
  • Fixed principal: the principal part never changes, the interest part falls.
  • Fixed principal costs a little less interest, but starts with a bigger payment.

Facilities: equipment up to 8 years (financing up to 90%), commercial property up to 30 years, working capital up to 5 years unsecured. Factoring pays up to 80 to 90%.

qs.q: A loan has an annual rate of 8% with monthly payments over 3 years. What are r and n?
qs.exp: r = annual rate / 12 = 8% / 12 = 0.6667% per month. n = years x 12 = 36 months. Always convert both to months.

qs.q: Which formula gives a fixed monthly instalment?
o: A = P x r x n
qs.exp: Fixed (equal) instalment: A = P x r / [1 - (1 + r)^-n]. The other forms are wrong: P / n is the fixed principal part only.

qs.q: In a fixed principal loan, what is the monthly principal repayment?
qs.exp: Fixed principal: R = P / n. The instalment changes each month because the interest part falls as the balance falls.

qs.q: In a fixed principal loan, how is the interest for a given month worked out?
o: Original loan x r, every month
Balance before that month's payment x r
Principal repayment x r, every month
qs.exp: Interest = outstanding balance before that payment x r. The instalment for month k = R + balance x r, and the balance falls by R each month.

qs.q: Which gives the total interest for a fixed instalment loan?
qs.exp: Total interest = total paid - principal = A x n - P. Forgetting to subtract P is a common mistake.

qs.q: Which formula gives the total interest for a fixed principal loan?
qs.exp: Total interest = r x R x n(n+1)/2. Or take the average of the first and last month's interest and multiply by n.

qs.q: A student works out a fixed instalment on a $200,000, 9% p.a., 20-year loan with monthly payments using r = 9% and n = 20. What went wrong?
o: Nothing, the formula allows annual figures
r and n must both be monthly: r = 0.75% and n = 240
qs.exp: With monthly payments r and n must be monthly: r = 9% / 12 = 0.75% and n = 20 x 12 = 240. Both were wrong.

qs.q: A $150,000 loan at 6% p.a. is repaid in 12 equal monthly instalments (monthly rest). What is the monthly instalment in dollars? Give 2 decimal places.
For that loan (instalment $12,909.96 over 12 months, principal $150,000), what is the total interest in dollars? Give 2 decimal places.
qs.exp: Total paid = 12,909.96 x 12 = 154,919.52 (4,919.57 with the unrounded instalment). Total interest = total paid - P = about 4,919.57.

qs.q: A $500,000 loan at 12% p.a. is repaid in 36 equal monthly instalments (monthly rest). What is the monthly instalment in dollars? Give 2 decimal places.
For the loan of $500,000 at 12% p.a. over 36 months with a monthly instalment of $16,607.15, what is the total interest in dollars? Give 2 decimal places.
qs.exp: Total paid = 16,607.15 x 36 = 597,857.40 (97,857.58 with the unrounded instalment). Total interest = about 97,857.6.

qs.q: A $120,000 loan at 12% p.a. is repaid over 12 months with a fixed principal each month. What is the monthly principal repayment in dollars? Give 2 decimal places.
A $120,000 loan at 12% p.a. is repaid over 12 months with a fixed principal of $10,000 a month. What is the first month's instalment in dollars? Give 2 decimal places.
qs.hint: Interest is on the balance, which is the full loan in month 1.

qs.q: Same loan ($120,000, 12% p.a., 12 months, fixed principal $10,000). What is the second month's instalment in dollars? Give 2 decimal places.
Same loan. What is the last (12th) instalment in dollars? Give 2 decimal places.
qs.exp: Before the last payment the balance is 10,000. Last = 10,000 + 10,000 x 0.01 = 10,100.00.

qs.q: Same loan. What is the total interest over 12 months in dollars? Give 2 decimal places.
A $360,000 loan at 8% p.a. is repaid over 36 months with a fixed principal each month. What is the first month's instalment in dollars? Give 2 decimal places.
Same loan ($360,000, 8% p.a., 36 months, fixed principal). What is the total interest in dollars? Give 2 decimal places.

A $150,000 loan at 6% p.a. over 12 months has total interest of about $4,919.57 with fixed instalments. With fixed principal the total interest is $4,875.00. How much cheaper in dollars is fixed principal? Give 2 decimal places.
qs.exp: 4,919.57 - 4,875.00 = 44.57. Fixed principal is cheaper because the balance falls faster, but its early instalments are higher.

qs.q: Which tenor is correct for equipment financing?
o: Up to 30 years, financing up to 90%
Up to 8 years, financing up to 90%
qs.exp: Equipment up to 8 years with financing up to 90%. Commercial property up to 30 years. Working capital up to 5 years unsecured.

qs.q: Which statement about an overdraft or revolving credit is correct?
o: Fixed repayment dates and no redrawing
Draw up to a limit, repay and redraw, with the bank having little control over usage
Always secured on the borrower's house
qs.exp: Revolving credit and overdraft: draw up to a limit, repay and redraw, priced at prime plus a margin, reviewed yearly, and the bank has little control over usage.
